Hello! Welcome to Voat!

Privacytools is a fantastic resource. Read over it and look at your options. How far do you want to go?

I'd start off by getting some privacy and ad-blocking browser add-ons. uBlock Origin and Disconnect or Privacy Badger would be a good start. If you want to step it up a bit, get Random Agent Spoofer and HTTPS Everywhere.

Next thing you should do is get a password manager. If you don't want anything cloud-based, KeePass(X) would be fine; otherwise, get LastPass or Dashlane.

Email would depend on what you want. Tutanota would be good for most people, but they do not offer 2FA yet (deal breaker personally). If you don't mind spending ~$15/year, Posteo or Mailbox.org are very good.

Other than this, see my list of resources. It's geared toward PC monitoring programs, but you may find it useful.

Teach me, Sensei. :-)

Couldn't have asked for a better list of resources, and it covers a good chunk* of what I want to understand about computers. I feel like I can get started now. Thanks!

*The rest would be moving towards Linux and coding, though I do have an IRL spirit guide for that waiting in the wings. Also, crawl -> walk -> run.

Edit: I want to go as far as I can, starting somewhere reasonable. Looking at all your options. Edit2: Can't pay for much right now, but eventually. :-)

There are a lot of free options available; only limit is a good VPN option (never go free). If you don't want one though, not a problem.

Definitely grab the browser add-ons and start looking at password managers - that is about the easiest/quickest start. Lastpass or Dashlane, for example, makes it pretty easy to change passwords and can generate them for you. uBlock will get rid of most ads and stop some tracking (enable MVPS Hosts script).

Changing email could be more difficult. Tutanota, along with openmailbox, are both free and good, though. Also Protonmail, but they are currently invite-only (request an invite now, if you want one).

For any encryption, use VeraCrypt.

As for Linux, Mint (Cinnamon) is what I recommend for a beginner. It has a nice interface and it's easy to work with - spin up a VM with VirtualBox if you want to give it a shot.

You could go deeper into anonymity/security, but start with the basics first. Don't overwhelm yourself :)
